function: Hierarchical PPO: RP-agent allocates RISs to operators; OP-agents jointly learn BS beamforming, RIS phase shifts, and BS-user association to maximize sum-rate (p. 1, 6).
system: Downlink multi-RIS multi-operator: 2 operators with 2 BSs (10 antennas) each, 5 single-antenna users per operator, 4 reflecting RISs of 20 elements, frequency-selective; band not stated (p. 3, 10).
method: Hierarchical deep reinforcement learning (HPPO): LSTM+FC actor-critic RP-agent and FC actor-critic OP-agents with Beta policies, trained online by PPO; S-HPPO decomposes RIS allocation sequentially (p. 7-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rician fading (factor 10), path-loss exponents 2.5 (BS-RIS), 2.8 (RIS-user), 3.5 (BS-user), random BS and user positions; no dataset (p. 4, 10).
test_conditions: Online RL in a simulated environment; sum-rate convergence per setting (RIS elements, BSs, Rician factor, OPs) and sum-rate versus power and RIS counts; no unseen-condition test (p. 10-13).
baselines: Auction [21], distance, random and greedy RIS allocation with PPO at OPs; no-RIS PPO; centralized PPO; DDQN, SAC and DDPG variants within HDRL; 1D-HPPO (p. 10-13).
metrics: Sum-rate (bps/Hz) convergence and versus transmit power, RIS elements and RIS count; update and inference running time (p. 10-13).
complexity: Inference and update complexity orders for HPPO and S-HPPO (p. 9-10); S-HPPO 318% update and 221% inference improvement; HPPO about 10^8 RP-level parameters at L=11 (p. 13).
q1_support: p. 4: "All sub-channels follow Rician fading" - custom simulator with its own path-loss model; no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "we verify the stability of the HPPO algorithm under various environmental settings" - each setting has its own training curve (Figs. 6-9); no model trained in one condition and tested in an unseen one is reported.
q3_support: p. 11: "we implement soft actor-critic (SAC) and deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithms"; p. 11: "Random scheme: At each episode, the RP does not accept any information uploaded by the OPs and instead randomly allocates RISs to OPs"
q4_support: p. 9: "Table I compares the computational complexity of the inference phase for S-HPPO and HPPO"
q5_support: p. 10: "We consider a multi-RIS multi-OP network, where BSs are randomly distributed along a semicircular region" - self-generated simulation; no code or data link and no public dataset are stated.
notes: Included under the rule that a work learning a physical-layer decision jointly with an above-PHY one passes: the RP-level RIS allocation is network management, but the OP-agents learn beamforming and RIS phase shifts (p. 6); area 3. q3 rests on DDQN, SAC and DDPG variants inside the HDRL framework (Fig. 10, p. 11) plus auction, distance, random and greedy allocation baselines compared on sum-rate (Figs. 11-14); reviewer to confirm the DRL variants count as standard learning algorithms rather than variants of the proposed method.
